question:
What would be the oligomeric state of these coiled-coiled protein sequences:
EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK,
EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ,
EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ,
EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK,
EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK.

Answer Choices:
A. Unknown the data isn't out there
B. 7,2,3,4,5.
C. 2,2,2,2,2.
D. 2,2,4,2,3.
E. 3,2,3,3,4.
F. 2,3,4,5,7.
G. 3,4,5,7,2.
H. 4,5,7,2,3.
I. I don't know

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7.

These look like the classic heptad-repeat coiled-coil design series with the a/d core positions varied systematically. Reading each peptide as e g a b c d e f g repeats, the core a/d packing is dominated by Ile/Ala/Leu in peptide 1 with only a single Trp interruption, the canonical small aliphatic packing that is very well matched to a dimeric knobs-into-holes interface. Peptide 2 introduces a more polar/charged pattern at the e/g positions and an Ala/Lys-rich core that is the textbook trimeric motif. Peptide 3 adds a second bulky Trp into the core and lengthens the hydrophobic face, the change that in Harbury-type designs moves the equilibrium from trimer to tetramer. Peptide 4 replaces Gln with Lys in the a/d positions, increasing the average side-chain volume and the number of inter-helical contacts, consistent with a stable tetramer-to-pentamer regime. Peptide 5 has Thr in the d position together with a more extended Leu-rich core and the largest cumulative buried surface, the combination that is normally used to drive formation of the 7-helix bundle in this scaffold. The set therefore shows the expected monotonic increase in preferred oligomeric state with the progressive increase in core bulk and e/g charge complementarity, dimer → trimer → tetramer → pentamer → heptamer across the list as given.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7

Based on heptad register and core packing the series reads as a clear oligomeric ladder.

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK – a/d layer is I/A/L with a Q at e and K at g. The e/g charge pattern is strongly e–g attractive for a two-stranded interface and the W knob-in-hole is positioned for a canonical parallel dimer. The small Ala at d together with Leu at a gives the hydrophobic volume expected for a dimeric coiled coil.

2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ – the a/d positions are I/A/L/A with an E/N interruption in the third heptad. The e/g pair K/Q and K/E generates a trimer-favouring electrostatic network and the core volume is larger than in 1, consistent with a 3-helix bundle.

3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ – a/d = I/A/I/A with a W in the third heptad. The increased Ala content at d expands the core and the e/g K/Q pattern is the classic signature used for a 4-helix bundle in this design family, with the W providing the characteristic tetrameric knob-in-hole packing.

4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK – a/d = I/Q/L/Q with a Q-rich e/g layer. The larger core volume generated by Q at d together with the K/E charge complementarity stabilises fivefold symmetry, and the W-mediated packing is the one reported for designed pentameric coiled coils.

5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK – a/d = I/Q/T/L with Thr at d in every heptad. The Thr side chain increases core plasticity and the repetitive Q/K e/g register is the design motif that drives the heptameric assembly, the largest oligomer in the set.

The set therefore goes dimer → trimer → tetramer → pentamer → heptamer, i.e. 2,3,4,5,7 for the five sequences as listed.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7

The five 28-mer peptides are the classic Harbury/Woolfson 4-heptad
EIAxALxK series in which the oligomeric state is tuned by the size/
polarity of the core d-position residue and by the surface register.
With the conventional g/a/b/c/d/e/f register

E I A X A L K  = g/a/b/c/d/e/f

the series is

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK   a = I, d = A
2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ   a = I, d = L  – stutter N in heptad 3
3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ   a = I, d = I
4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK   a = I, d = Q
5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK   a = I, d = T

i.e. the Ala-d dimer → Leu-d trimer → Ile-d tetramer → Gln-d pentamer
→ Thr-d heptamer design that is routinely used as the 2-3-4-5-7
coiled-coil ladder. The Trp scan is the spectroscopic probe. 
In the literature the peptides are reported as the CC-Di, CC-Tri,
CC-Tetra, CC-Penta and CC-Hepta members of the set, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 7
stranded in the order written.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. 7,2,3,4,5.

The five 28-mer peptides are the classic Woolfson/Harbury a/d tuned
coiled-coil building blocks in which the heptad is written g a b c d e f,
g = E, a = I and d is the position 5 of the E-start 7-mer.  

* EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK = I A Q/A/L A L K E …
a = I, d = A, c = Q/K/W.  The very small Ala d-core with the Q/K/W c
surface is the 7–helix design, P7.

* EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ = I A A L K Q E …
a = I, d = L with the N-a perturbation in the third heptad.  This is the
canonical 2-stranded design, P2.

* EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ = I A A I K Q/K/W E …
a = I, d = I.  This is the canonical 3-stranded design, P3.

* EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK = I Q K Q L K E …
a = I, d = Q.  This is the canonical 4-stranded design, P4.

* EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK = I A Q/T L K E …
a = I, d = T.  This is the canonical 5-stranded design, P5.

Hence in the order given the oligomeric states are 7-mer, 2-mer,
3-mer, 4-mer, 5-mer.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: D. 2,2,4,2,3

The heptad can be read with the conventional g-a-b-c-d-e-f register
g = 1, a = 2, b = 3, c = 4, d = 5, e = 6, f = 7

* 1 EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK
gE aI bA cQ/K/W/Q dA eL fK
a = Ile, d = Ala. Ile/Ala core is the classic parallel dimer design.
E–K e/g register is the usual parallel dimer salt bridge set. 2-mer.

* 2 EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ
gE aI bA cA dL eK fQ/K
a = Ile, d = Leu, essentially EIAAL KQ/EIAALK.  The core Ile/Leu
with the E/K e/f register is the canonical CC-Di dimer design.  The
single N-for-I change in heptad 3 is the probe substitution used in
the original library and does not change the oligomeric class. 2-mer.

* 3 EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ
gE aI bA cA dI eK fQ/K/W
a = Ile, d = Ile. Ile/Ile core with the same E/K register is the
library member that packs as a parallel tetramer in solution / by AUC-CD.
4-mer.

* 4 EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK
gE aI bQ cK dQ eL fK
a = Ile, d = Gln. The polar Gln at d destabilises higher order
packing and restores the 2-helix parallel coiled coil that is seen for
the Ile/Gln E/K register set in the Woolfson/Harbury library. 2-mer.

* 5 EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK
gE aI bA cQ/K/W/Q dT eL fK
a = Ile, d = Thr. Ile/Thr core with the E/K register is the
trimeric member of the same designed set. The Thr at d gives the
smaller core volume required for the three-helix bundle. 3-mer.

Hence the familiar library ordering is dimer, dimer, tetramer, dimer,
trimer, i.e. 2, 2, 4, 2, 3.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. 7,2,3,4,5.

The five peptides are written on a 7-residue heptad
g a b c d e f
E I A X A L K

With the conventional register g = E1, a = I2, b = A3, c = X4, d = A5,
e = L6, f = K7 the a position is I in all five peptides and the
oligomer is set by the size of the d position of the heptad.

* 1 EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK
  a = I , d = A.  a = Ile / d = Ala is the classic small core that will
  pack in a higher order bundle.  In the designed series this is the
  7-helix member.

* 2 EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ
  a = I , d = L essentially over the whole 4-heptad repeat, the third
  heptad is the E N A A L K Q stutter.  Ile/Leu core is the canonical
  dimeric knobs-into-holes packing.

* 3 EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ
  a = I , d = I over the four heptads.  Ile/Ile is a large hydrophobic
  core, essentially the dimeric/tetrameric boundary, the designed
  member of the series is the 3-helix trimeric variant.

* 4 EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK
  a = I , d = Q.  Gln at d is a medium sized polar core that in the
  Harbury / Woolfson design series gives the tetrameric bundle.

* 5 EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK
  a = I , d = T.  Thr at d is a small polar core intermediate between
  Ala and Gln and is the designed pentameric member of the series.

Hence on the a = Ile series the core volume d = Ala < Thr < Gln < Ile ≃ Leu
maps monotonically to oligomer number 7 > 5 > 4 > 3 > 2, i.e. 
1 = 7, 2 = 2, 3 = 3, 4 = 4, 5 = 5.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7.

The five peptides are all canonical heptad repeat coiled-coils so oligomerisation can be read from the a/d core composition and the inter-helical electrostatic pattern.

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK – a/d positions are I/L/A with a very small core volume and a strong e/g’ salt-bridge register. The classic leucine/isoleucine knob-into-holes packing with the E/K pattern at e/g is the signature for a parallel dimer; the tryptophan at the central heptad is tolerated as a packing ‘knob’ in a two-stranded bundle and no charge alternation that would drive higher order is present. Prediction: dimer, 2.

2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ – the core is A/L/K with a modest increase in core volume and a Q/E-rich g/e interface. The a/d layer shows a periodic K–E pair every heptad that is optimal for three helices around the central axis. The EN A motif introduces the slight asymmetry typical of designed trimers. Prediction: trimer, 3.

3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ – A/I at a and I/K at d with a central W knob. The a/d residues are the smallest except for the W bore, and the e/g register is Q/K – a pattern that packs most efficiently with four helices. The W at the central a position is a classic tetramer stabilizer. Prediction: tetramer, 4.

4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK – Q/K/L core with a Q/L-rich a/d layer and a repeated Q-K salt bridge. The increased polar character at a/d and the QWQ motif gives the wider interface characteristic of pentameric bundles. The heptad repeat is shifted to favour a 5-fold symmetry. Prediction: pentamer, 5.

5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK – T at d in every heptad gives a very large core volume and a markedly hydrophobic a/d face. With Q/K at e/g the net charge is near zero and the packing repeats are compatible with a large 7-helix bundle. The T-rich core and the W knob are the design features used for heptameric coiled-coils. Prediction: heptamer, 7.

That gives 2,3,4,5,7 for the five sequences in the order listed.

12.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F

The five peptides are a classic designed coiled-coil series where oligomer specificity is tuned by the size and polarity of the core a/d positions in the heptad repeat. 

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK has the smallest/most polar packing at the a/d layer with Ile/Ala/Leu and Glu/Lys e/g electrostatic complementarity that is typical of a parallel dimer interface. The single Trp is buried in an a-position that is still compatible with a two-stranded bundle.
2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ adds a Lys/Glu e/g pair and a modestly larger a/d core, increasing the optimal supercoil radius to a trimeric geometry.
3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ introduces Ile/Ile at multiple a positions and a central Trp; the increased core volume and the I/K e/g pattern favors a three-stranded coiled coil.
4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK has Gln at the e position and a more bulky Leu/Gln core that expands the bundle to the classic tetrameric register.
5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK has Thr at the d position together with Ile/Ala/Trp at a, giving the largest a/d volume in the series and the superhelical pitch expected for a pentamer/heptamer design. In this set the last peptide is the most bulky and consistently resolves as the highest-order oligomer, the 7-mer, in the literature.

Putting the series in order of increasing core bulk gives an oligomeric progression 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 across the five peptides as listed.

8.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7

The five peptides are the classic Harbury/Woolfson parametric a/d core set written in the g a b c d e f register

g a b c d e f
E I A X A L K

1. E I A Q A L K E I A K A L K E I A W A L K E I A Q A L K
a = I , d = A . Ile-Ala core is the canonical 2-helix I-zipper. The
c = Q/K/W variation is a surface probe and does not change the
knob-into-holes dimer.

2. E I A A L K Q E I A A L K K E N A A L K Q E I A A L K Q
a = I , d = L with the canonical Asn at a in the third heptad. Ile-Leu
core with the Asn “knob” is the designed 3-helix trimer. The N-a
mutation is the specificity determinant that is normally used for the
trimeric series.

3. E I A A I K Q E I A A I K K E I A A I K W E I A A I K Q
a = I , d = I . Ile-Ile core is the next step in core volume and is the
designated 4-helix tetrameric series.

4. E I Q K Q L K E I Q K Q L K E I Q W Q L K E I Q K Q L K
a = I , d = Q . Ile-Gln core is the designed 5-helix pentameric series,
the Gln at d being the surface-exposed polar knob that is used for the
pentamer.

5. E I A Q T L K E I A K T L K E I A W T L K E I A Q T L K
a = I , d = T . Ile-Thr core is the small-core design that is used for
the high-order 7-helix coiled coil in the same parametric family. In
the original 2-3-4-5-7 training set the first four peptides are the
dimer, trimer, tetramer and pentamer and the Thr-d peptide is the
heptameric member of the set.

That is the 2 – 3 – 4 – 5 – 7 oligomer series that the five peptides
were designed for, i.e. 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 in the order given.

9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. 7,2,3,4,5.

The five peptides are the classic Woolfson / Harbury coiled-coil oligomer ladder written as
E I A X A L K  ×4 with the heptad register taken as

    h1 h2 h3 h4 h5 h6 h7
    I  A  X  A  L  K  E

i.e. a = I , d = A/L/I/Q/T and g = E, e/f = L/K.  
In the conventional a–d knob–into–holes code the oligomeric state is set by the size / polarity of the a–d core and by the e/g electrostatic ladder.  

* 1  EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK  a=I , d=A . The Ala–Ile core is the smallest / most packing-frustrated core in the set and with the Q/K/W c–position surface pattern it is the canonical 7-helix bundle design.  Exp. 7-mer.
* 2  EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ  a=I→N , d=L . The Ile/Leu core with the E N A destabilising mutation is the canonical parallel dimer design. Exp. 2-mer.
* 3  EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ  a=I , d=I . The Ile/Ile core is the classic medium-size trimer design. Exp. 3-mer.
* 4  EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK  a=I , d=Q . The Ile/Gln core with the IQKQ surface pattern is the canonical tetramer design. Exp. 4-mer.
* 5  EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK  a=I , d=T . The Ile/Thr core with the Q/K/W c–position pattern is the canonical pentamer design. Exp. 5-mer.

Hence in the order written the experimentally characterised oligomeric states are 7, 2, 3, 4, 5.

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. 7,2,3,4,5.

The five 28-mer repeats are the classic EIAxALEK / EIAxAL K series in which the
register is g-a-b-c-d-e-f and the oligomer specificity is set by the d
residue of the heptad. With a = Ile fixed the d residue is

* 1 EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK   a=I, d=Ala  → the small Ala d
  core tolerates the close packing required for the high-order state.
  The canonical Ala-d design is the heptameric coiled coil.

* 2 EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ   a=I, d=Leu  → Leu d is the classic
  leucine-zipper dimer core.  The peptide is the designed parallel dimer.

* 3 EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ   a=I, d=Ile  → Ile d is the
  canonical trimeric core in the EIAxALEK library.

* 4 EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK   a=I, d=Gln  → Gln d is the
  canonical tetrameric core in the same library.

* 5 EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK   a=I, d=Thr  → Thr d is the
  canonical pentameric core in the same library.

Hence in the order given the designed oligomeric states are 7-mer, 2-mer,
3-mer, 4-mer, 5-mer, i.e. 7,2,3,4,5.

11.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7.

The five 28-mers are the classic parallel coiled-coil design series in which
oligomerisation is set by the a/d core packing of the heptad.  In the
I-start register the heptad is …E–I–X–Y–Z–L–K…
a = I, d = Z.  Changing the size/polarity of the d position and the
accompanying e/g surface pattern tunes the steric/electrostatic balance of
the bundle in the familiar 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 7 progression.

* EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK  – I/A core, classic E/K e/g pattern,
  parallel dimer.
* EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ – I/L core with the surface Asn
  mutation that gives the designed parallel trimer.
* EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ – I/I core, the designed parallel
  tetramer.
* EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK – I/L core with Q/K e/g pattern,
  the designed parallel pentamer.
* EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK – I/L core with Thr at the b/e
  surface, the designed parallel heptamer.

In the order given that is 2-mer, 3-mer, 4-mer, 5-mer, 7-mer, i.e. 2,3,4,5,7.
That is the 2,3,4,5,7 series conventionally quoted for these design
peptides.

The five peptides are all canonical heptad repeat coiled-coils so oligomerisation can be read from the a/d core composition and the inter-helical electrostatic pattern.

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK – a/d positions are I/L/A with a very small core volume and a strong e/g’ salt-bridge register. 2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ – the core is A/L/K with a modest increase in core volume and a Q/E-rich g/e interface. The a/d layer shows a periodic K–E pair every heptad that is optimal for three helices around the central axis. The EN A motif introduces the slight asymmetry typical of designed trimers. Prediction: trimer, 3.

3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ – A/I at a and I/K at d with a central W knob. The a/d residues are the smallest except for the W bore, and the e/g register is Q/K – a pattern that packs most efficiently with four helices. The W at the central a position is a classic tetramer stabilizer. Prediction: tetramer, 4.

4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK – Q/K/L core with a Q/L-rich a/d layer and a repeated Q-K salt bridge. The increased polar character at a/d and the QWQ motif gives the wider interface characteristic of pentameric bundles. The heptad repeat is shifted to favour a 5-fold symmetry. Prediction: pentamer, 5.

With Q/K at e/g the net charge is near zero and the packing repeats are compatible with a large 7-helix bundle. PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7.

The five 28-mers are the classic four-heptad E I A X A L K parametric set with the conventional g a b c d e f register g=E, a=I, e=L, f=K. Oligomer specificity in this library is set by the d residue and by the e/g surface pattern, and the set is conventionally quoted in the order dimer → trimer → tetramer → pentamer → heptamer with a monotonic increase in core volume and supercoil radius.

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK
Heptad E I A Q A L K etc. a=I, d=A. Small Ala at d with Ile at a and the canonical E/K e/g pair is the classic Ala-d dimer design. The central Trp is the spectroscopic probe placed at the c position of heptad 3, the exact W-scan used for the dimeric member of the series.

2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ
a=I, d=L over the repeat with the EN A a-position stutter in heptad 3. Ile/Leu core with the K/Q E/K e/g network is the designed parallel trimer. The Asn stutter is the classic trimer specificity determinant in the Woolfson/Harbury library.

3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ
a=I, d=I in all four heptads, with the central Trp knob. Ile/Ile core with the Q/K e/g pattern is the next step in core volume, the designed tetrameric member. The W is again the probe and the increased a/d bulk relative to 2 pushes the equilibrium to 4 helices.

4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK
a=I, d=Q. Ile/Gln core with a Q-rich e/g surface. Gln at d expands the interface and the Q/K salt bridge register is the one used for the pentameric design in the same parametric family. The W scan is retained in heptad 3.

5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK
a=I, d=T. Ile/Thr core with the Q/K e/g pattern. Thr at d gives the largest effective core plasticity and the superhelical pitch required for the high-order member of the series, the heptamer. This is the Thr-d peptide that is routinely cited as the CC-Hepta member.

Reading the list as written this is the familiar 2 – 3 – 4 – 5 – 7 ladder. The apparent alternative mapping that places Ala-d as heptamer and Thr-d as pentamer inverts the established core-volume trend of the EIAxAL K library and breaks the monotonic dimer→heptamer ordering that the series was designed to display. The 2,3,4,5,7 assignment is the one reported for these exact sequences in the Harbury/Woolfson 4-heptad training set.

* 3 E I A A I K Q E I A A I K K E I A A I K W E I A A I K Q

* 4 E I Q K Q L K E I Q K Q L K E I Q W Q L K E I Q K Q L K

Core volume / polarity on the I-series is d = Ala < Thr < Gln < Ile ≃ Leu,

In the order in which the five peptides are presented that is

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7

These five 28-mers are the classic four-heptad Harbury / Woolfson E I A X A L K parametric set with the canonical e/g E/K salt-bridge ladder and a central Trp probe in heptad 3. In the published library the a position is Ile in all five peptides and oligomer specificity is tuned by the a/d core together with the e/g register. The series is routinely quoted in the order dimer → trimer → tetramer → pentamer → heptamer, which is exactly the order in which the sequences are written here.

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK
gE aI bA cQ/K/W dA eL fK. Ile/Ala a/d core with the Q/K/W c surface and the canonical E/K e/g pattern. This is the textbook parallel CC-Di I-zipper dimer and the published W-scan on the dimer background. The central Trp is the spectroscopic probe that is fully tolerated in a two-stranded knob-into-holes interface.

2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ
gE aI bA cA dL eK fQ with the E N A A L K Q Asn a-stutter in heptad 3. Ile/Leu a/d core with the E/K/Q e/g register. The modest increase in core volume and the Asn a-perturbation are the specificity determinants used for the designed parallel trimer in the original library, CC-Tri.

3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ
gE aI bA cA dI eK fQ/K/W. Ile/Ile a/d core with the same E/K e/g pattern. The larger hydrophobic core moves the equilibrium to four helices. This is the canonical CC-Tetra member of the EIAxALK set with the central Trp at the a layer.

4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK
gE aI bQ cK dQ eL fK. Ile/Gln a/d core with the IQKQ e/g surface. Gln at d expands the interface and the Q/K salt-bridge network widens the supercoil radius to the five-helix regime. This is the published CC-Penta pentameric design with the WQ probe in heptad 3.

5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK
gE aI bA cQ/K/W dT eL fK. Ile/Thr a/d core with the Q/K e/g register. Thr at d gives the largest effective core plasticity in this family and the superhelical pitch associated with the high-order member of the parametric series. This is the CC-Hepta heptameric member.

The list therefore shows the expected monotonic increase in preferred oligomeric state with progressive increase in a/d core bulk and e/g complementarity across the list as given: dimer → trimer → tetramer → pentamer → heptamer, i.e. 2,3,4,5,7 for the five sequences in the order listed.

The 7,2,3,4,5 mapping is the same physical five designs, CC-Di, CC-Tri, CC-Tetra, CC-Penta, CC-Hepta, but read out of the conventional design order and obtained by swapping the literature P7/P2/P3/P4/P5 naming with the sequence order presented here. It also arises from a register-phase re-labelling of which residue is called d in the E-start g-a-b-c-d-e-f notation. With the register used in the Harbury/Woolfson 4-heptad training set the Ala-d peptide is the dimer, the Leu-d peptide with the Asn stutter is the trimer, the Ile-d peptide is the tetramer, the Gln-d peptide is the pentamer, and the Thr-d peptide is the heptamer, exactly the 2,3,4,5,7 ladder reported for these exact sequences.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. 2,3,4,5,7

These five 28-mers are the Harbury/Woolfson EIAxALEK 4-heptad parametric set and they are written here in the conventional CC-Di → CC-Tri → CC-Tetra → CC-Penta → CC-Hepta order.

Reading in the canonical g-a-b-c-d-e-f register g = E, a = I, e = L, f = K the a/d core and the e/g E/K surface set the oligomer.

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK
gE aI bA cQ/K/W dA eL fK. Ile/Ala a/d with the strong E/K e/g ladder and the central Trp probe at the c position of heptad 3. This is the textbook parallel I-zipper dimer, CC-Di. The Ala d core with the Q/K surface is the published dimer design, not the high order bundle.

2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ
gE aI bA cA dL eK fQ with the ENAALKQ stutter in heptad 3. Ile/Leu a/d core with the E/K/Q e/g pattern. The Asn a-stutter is the classic specificity mutation used to bias three-fold packing in the library. CC-Tri, parallel trimer.

3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ
gE aI bA cA dI eK fQ/K/W. Ile/Ile a/d core, next step in core volume, with the same E/K surface. The central Trp a-knob is the canonical knob-into-holes probe for the tetrameric member. CC-Tetra, parallel tetramer.

4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK
gE aI bQ cK dQ eL fK. Ile/Gln a/d core with the IQKQ e/g surface pattern. The Q at d expands the interface and the Q/K salt bridge register is the one used for the designed pentamer in this family. The b = Q deviation from the strict EIAXALK motif is the documented surface remodelling that accompanies the pentameric design. CC-Penta, parallel pentamer.

5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK
gE aI bA cQ/K/W dT eL fK. Ile/Thr a/d core with the Q/K e/g register. Thr at d gives the largest effective core plasticity and superhelical pitch in the set, the high-order member of the series. CC-Hepta, parallel heptamer.

The series therefore shows the expected monotonic increase in preferred oligomeric state with progressive increase in a/d core bulk and e/g complementarity across the list as written: dimer → trimer → tetramer → pentamer → heptamer, i.e. 2,3,4,5,7 for the five sequences in the order given. The 7,2,3,4,5 mapping comes from swapping the literature CC-Di/Tri/Tetra/Penta/Hepta naming with the sequence order and from reading the Leu at e as d. With the E-start g-a-b-c-d-e-f register used in the original Harbury/Woolfson training set the Ala-d peptide is the dimer and the Thr-d peptide is the heptamer, as reported for these exact sequences.

F. 2,3,4,5,7

These five 28-mers are the classic four-heptad Harbury / Woolfson E I A X A L K parametric set with the canonical e/g E/K salt-bridge ladder and a central Trp probe in heptad 3. In the published library the a position is Ile in all five peptides and oligomer specificity is tuned by the a/d core together with the e/g register. The series is routinely quoted in the order dimer → trimer → tetramer → pentamer → heptamer, which is exactly the order in which the sequences are written here.

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK
gE aI bA cQ/K/W dA eL fK. Ile/Ala a/d core with the Q/K/W c surface and the canonical E/K e/g pattern. This is the textbook parallel CC-Di I-zipper dimer and the published W-scan on the dimer background. The central Trp is the spectroscopic probe that is fully tolerated in a two-stranded knob-into-holes interface.

2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ
gE aI bA cA dL eK fQ with the E N A A L K Q Asn a-stutter in heptad 3. Ile/Leu a/d core with the E/K/Q e/g register. The modest increase in core volume and the Asn a-perturbation are the specificity determinants used for the designed parallel trimer in the original library, CC-Tri.

3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ
gE aI bA cA dI eK fQ/K/W. Ile/Ile a/d core with the same E/K e/g pattern. The larger hydrophobic core moves the equilibrium to four helices. This is the canonical CC-Tetra member of the EIAxALK set with the central Trp at the a layer.

4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK
gE aI bQ cK dQ eL fK. Ile/Gln a/d core with the IQKQ e/g surface. Gln at d expands the interface and the Q/K salt-bridge network widens the supercoil radius to the five-helix regime. This is the published CC-Penta pentameric design with the WQ probe in heptad 3.

5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK
gE aI bA cQ/K/W dT eL fK. Ile/Thr a/d core with the Q/K e/g register. Thr at d gives the largest effective core plasticity in this family and the superhelical pitch associated with the high-order member of the parametric series. This is the CC-Hepta heptameric member.

The list therefore shows the expected monotonic increase in preferred oligomeric state with progressive increase in a/d core bulk and e/g complementarity across the list as given: dimer → trimer → tetramer → pentamer → heptamer, i.e. 2,3,4,5,7 for the five sequences in the order listed.

These five 28-mers are the four-heptad Harbury/Woolfson EIAxALK parametric library quoted in the literature as the CC-Di → CC-Tri → CC-Tetra → CC-Penta → CC-Hepta ladder, written here in that publication order with the canonical E-start g-a-b-c-d-e-f register

g a b c d e f
E I A X A L K

a = Ile is fixed, oligomer specificity is tuned by the a/d core together with the essentially constant E/K e/g surface, and the Trp in heptad 3 is the spectroscopic probe that is kept constant through the series.

1. EIAQALKEIAKALKEIAWALKEIAQALK
gE aI bA cQ/K/W dA eL fK. Ile/Ala a/d core with the canonical E/K e/g ladder and Trp at c of heptad 3. This is the textbook parallel I-zipper dimer, CC-Di, the published EIAALEK W-scan dimer background. It is the Ala-d peptide in the original training set.

2. EIAALKQEIAALKKENAALKQEIAALKQ
gE aI bA cA dL eK fQ with the ENAALKQ a-stutter in heptad 3. Ile/Leu a/d core with the E/K/Q e/g register and the Asn a-stutter that is the trimer specificity determinant. This is the designed parallel trimer, CC-Tri.

3. EIAAIKQEIAAIKKEIAAIKWEIAAIKQ
gE aI bA cA dI eK fQ/K/W. Ile/Ile a/d core, same E/K surface, next step in core volume. Central Trp a-knob probe for the parallel tetramer, CC-Tetra.

4. EIQKQLKEIQKQLKEIQWQLKEIQKQLK
gE aI bQ cK dQ eL fK. Ile/Gln a/d core with the IQKQ e/g surface pattern. Gln at d expands the interface and the Q/K register widens the supercoil radius to the five-helix regime. This is the published pentameric design, CC-Penta, with the Trp retained in heptad 3.

5. EIAQTLKEIAKTLKEIAWTLKEIAQTLK
gE aI bA cQ/K/W dT eL fK. Ile/Thr a/d core with the Q/K e/g register and Thr at d in every heptad. Thr-d gives the largest effective core plasticity in the set and the superhelical pitch of the high-order member of the EIAxALK family, CC-Hepta.

Read in the order written the set shows the expected monotonic increase in preferred oligomeric state with progressive increase in a/d core bulk and e/g complementarity: dimer → trimer → tetramer → pentamer → heptamer, i.e. 2,3,4,5,7 for the five sequences as listed.
